finding: classification_table builds the ProbLevel grid from the UNADJUSTED pd range, but SAS builds it from the bias-adjusted (leave-one-out) pstar range. Proven by a real SAS run: judge/runs/x_split_drift_m_metrics_threshold has pd in [0.000299, 0.857878] and pstar in [0.000299, 0.881482], and SAS printed 46 rows, 0.000..0.900. The module gives 44 rows, 0.000..0.860 (checked by running stepwise_logistic + classification_table on that run's features), so the file would fail on row count. The other 44 levels match SAS exactly. On the judged train input both ranges give 0.000..0.880, so the reference never shows the difference. The inventory row itself flagged this as untested ('pd vs pstar for the grid ends is untested'). Also, the +1e-9/-1e-9 fuzz inside floor/ceil (:735-736) is not in the inventory rule: pd = 0.04 - 1e-12 gives lo = 0.04 where the rule gives 0.02.
cites: inventory train.sas printed_classification.csv row (2) GRID 'from floor(min pd / 0.02)*0.02 to ceil(max pd / 0.02)*0.02 ... pd vs pstar for the grid ends is untested'; judge/runs/x_split_drift_m_metrics_threshold/printed_classification.csv (ProbLevel 0.880 and 0.900 rows); scratch sc-review-B/ctable_grid.py and ctable_drift_module.py
fix: lo = floor(min(pstar)/0.02)*0.02 and hi = ceil(max(pstar)/0.02)*0.02 using ps, not p, with no 1e-9 fuzz (or a fuzz justified in a TODO(port)). Amend the inventory row: the upper end is SAS-proven by x_split_drift. The lower end is unproven (both give 0.000), so add TODO(port) for min.

finding: sas_d8's E-notation branch always prints 3 significant digits (mant_dec=2). SAS's D8. E-notation fills width 8 and strips trailing zeros, exactly like BEST8. E-notation. SAS printed StdErr '6.321E-6' (m_fe_health_penalty), '6.418E-6' (m_fe_impute_mean), '3.341E-6' (m_fe_import_guessingrows), '6.409E-6' (m_fe_median_group_misaligned) and '6.444E-6' (m_train_slstay); the module prints '6.32E-6', '6.42E-6', '3.34E-6', '6.41E-6', '6.44E-6'. These are the only 6 of 1,245 SAS D8 cells across reference + 17 runs that sas_d8 fails to reproduce. StdErrs recomputed from SAS's own pd (6.3205993e-6, 6.4178796e-6, 3.3409826e-6, ...) under the width-8 rule reproduce all 7 SAS E cells, including the reference '6.42E-6' (SAS value 6.4204851e-6 -> '6.420' -> stripped) and '-9.88E-6'. The module matches the judged reference cell only by coincidence. The correct rule prints '6.421E-6' from the converged fit (6.4207195e-6), 7e-10 from SAS's '6.42E-6', well inside the judge's 2-display-unit StdErr tolerance (2e-8).
cites: inventory train.sas model_coefficients.csv (ODS ParameterEstimates) row ('E-notation with 3 significant digits ... f'{x:.2E}''; 'threshold is only bracketed'); judge/runs/{m_fe_health_penalty,m_fe_impute_mean,m_fe_import_guessingrows,m_fe_median_group_misaligned,m_train_slstay}/model_coefficients.csv; listings judge/runs/m_fe_health_penalty/train.sas.lst:1032 and judge/reference/listings/train.sas.lst:1073 (right-aligned width 8); scratch sc-review-B/formats.py, d8_e.py
fix: E branch: return _enotation(x, 8), i.e. the mantissa fills width 8 with trailing zeros stripped. That is the same text as sas_best(x, 8) for |x| < 1e-5. Amend the inventory row's D8 rule. The fixed branch is right (1,239/1,239 fixed cells reproduce).

finding: Chi-square p-values come from two hand-written closed forms (_sf1, and _chi2_sf for HL at :699). The rulebook allows scipy for exactly this, and the inventory rows name scipy.stats.chi2.sf. The numbers are right: max relative error vs scipy is 9.9e-14 (_chi2_sf, df 1..39, x up to 1,400) and 1.9e-13 (_sf1), and no PVALUE6.4 text differs. But it is a second mapping for one construct, and the df>1 version is private, yet it is what the global-tests p-value (chi-square(q)) needs. The check script already reaches into sc._chi2_sf (sas_compat_checks.py:383), and a train translator following the printed_global_tests.csv row would call scipy directly, giving two implementations. The answer is right, but the rule was quietly ignored.
cites: RULEBOOK §1 Numerics row ('scipy only for scipy.stats.chi2.sf (p-values)'); RULEBOOK §2 intro ('An implementer who invents a second mapping ... is violating a rule'); inventory train.sas printed_hosmer_lemeshow.csv row ('ProbChiSq = scipy.stats.chi2.sf(ChiSq, DF)') and printed_global_tests.csv row ('scipy.stats.chi2.sf, RULEBOOK §1'); scratch sc-review-B/chi2.py
fix: Expose one public helper, e.g. sas_compat.chi2_sf(x, df) = float(scipy.stats.chi2.sf(x, df)). Use it in stepwise_logistic (:519, :546) and hosmer_lemeshow (:699), and delete _sf1/_chi2_sf. The stepwise selection rule compares p with slentry, so keep the comparison on the p-value as now.

finding: classification_table(y, x, fit) does not have the inventory's signature classification_table(X, y, pd): the argument order is swapped and it takes a LogisticFit instead of pd. It also recomputes pd = 1/(1+exp(-x beta)) and uses fit.cov, where the inventory computes V = inverse(X' diag(w) X) from the given pd. A translator following the binding row gets a TypeError or a silent argument swap. The helper also cannot be fed SAS's own pd, so the inventory's byte-identical verification cannot be repeated through it. The check script therefore tests only the converged fit, at port tolerance (sas_compat_checks.py:411-417). The same formula fed SAS's pd reproduces printed_classification.csv exactly in 17 of 18 SAS runs (the 18th differs only by the B-01 grid). Amendment S4 (pending) covers return columns, not this signature.
cites: inventory train.sas printed_classification.csv row ('sas_compat.classification_table(X, y, pd) ... w = pd(1-pd); V = inverse(X' diag(w) X)'); RULEBOOK §5 (inventory decisions are binding); migration/stress-test/amendment-queue.md S4; scratch sc-review-B/ctable.py
fix: Signature classification_table(x, y, pd), with w and V computed from pd. Train passes the final model's pd, the same array it writes to risk_scores_train.csv. Alternatively, amend the inventory row first and cite the amendment in the docstring.

finding: roc_association(y, score) has no label parameter and returns a numeric dataclass. The three binding inventory rows specify roc_association(y=default_flag, score=pd_logistic, label='Training Set') returning ONE row with ROCModel as the first column. The docstring says 'the caller adds the ROCModel label', but no amendment sanctions this. S4 is pending and covers only HL/ctable/Association conventions. Train and metrics translators following their rows will call it with label= and fail, or each build the row their own way. The numbers are right: brute-force all-pairs C/D/T and DeLong components agree to 4e-19 on reference train/valid and edge a/b/c, and 51/51 SAS ROC files in judge/runs are reproduced text-identically.
cites: inventory train.sas printed_roc_train.csv, printed_roc_validation.csv and metrics_calculation.sas printed_roc_metrics.csv rows ('sas_compat.roc_association(y=..., score=..., label=...) -> ONE row, columns in this order: ROCModel, Area, ...'); amendment-queue.md S4; scratch sc-review-B/roc.py
fix: Add label: str and return the one-row frame (ROCModel, Area, StdErr, LowerArea, UpperArea, SomersD, Gamma, TauA) with full-precision floats. Or amend the three inventory rows before any translation relies on the current API.

finding: fit_logistic has no handling for separation or non-convergence. (a) Under quasi-complete separation the weights underflow to 0, X'WX becomes singular and np.linalg.solve raises LinAlgError. Repro: x = 50 zeros + 50 ones, y = 1 wherever x = 1. Both fit_logistic and stepwise_logistic then crash, where SAS warns and continues. (b) After 100 iterations (:415) it returns converged=False silently, and stepwise_logistic (:502-504, :522, :550) never checks .converged, so an unconverged fit drives the next score/Wald test without any flag. Neither case is reachable on the fixed train input: every step converges in 8 iterations, and no step-halving occurs on the reference.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 model fitting row (A17: 'to full convergence (max abs step < 1e-10)'); RULEBOOK §2 UNKNOWN rule (TODO(port) for undecided cases); scratch sc-review-B/edge_fit.py case (c)
fix: In stepwise_logistic, check fit.converged after every fit and raise, or mark TODO(port), with the step number. In fit_logistic, catch the singular solve and raise a clear error with a TODO(port) naming SAS's separation behaviour.

finding: Convergence is tested on the DAMPED step max|t*step|, not the Newton step. If all 40 halvings fail (:422-426), t = 2^-40, so any step with max|step| < 110 passes the 1e-10 test and the fit is reported converged=True even though it stalled. The halving test also accepts a -2 Log L increase up to 2e-12*|loglik| (:424), which A17 does not state. That slack is needed: my literal reading of A17 ('halve while -2 Log L increases', convergence on the full step) stalls at roundoff, looped 299 iterations and moved the step-1 score by 1.6e-3. But the slack is an unrecorded silence. On the 24 reference steps there are no halvings, and every beta matches my independent Newton to 7e-12.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 model fitting row (A17); RULEBOOK §2 UNKNOWN rule; scratch sc-review-B/stepwise_indep.py (first run vs second), halving.py (3 synthetic halving designs agree to 1e-15)
fix: Test convergence on max|step| (the undamped Newton step). Set converged=False if halving is exhausted. Document the 1e-12 relative roundoff slack as a TODO(port) or queue it as an A17 amendment.

finding: stepwise_logistic stops silently after 500 steps with no flag. The inventory stepwise row's TODO(port) (an effect whose alias is outside the model, if removed, could alternate with that alias) is not carried into the code at the alias test (:540). Neither is reachable: on all 7 distinct SAS stepwise inputs (reference, 5 feature-mutation runs, x_split_drift, plus slentry=0.10 and slstay=0.10 mutation runs) the module reproduces SAS's path exactly. Every chi-square is within 0.36 of the judge tolerance, and every ProbChiSq is text-identical except one fit-noise cell (m_train_slstay step 22: 0.1089 vs 0.1090).
cites: inventory train.sas 'work.logit_scored_train / model_coefficients / stepwise path' row ('TODO(port): if an effect with an alias outside the model were ever removed...'); RULEBOOK §3 marker format; scratch sc-review-B/stepwise_runs.py
fix: Add the inventory's TODO(port) at :540. At the cap, raise or add a TODO(port) instead of returning a truncated path.

finding: With fewer than 3 HL groups (heavy pd ties or tiny n), hosmer_lemeshow returns DF = NGroups - 2 <= 0 (even -1), a chi-square, and p = float('nan'). Repro: 2 groups gives (45.83, 0, nan). This breaks the module's own convention 'Missing numeric = polars null (never NaN)' (:5). What SAS prints when g < 3 is not decided anywhere. sas_pvalue(nan) happens to give ''. On every SAS input HL is byte-exact: partition and LackFitChiSq line text-identical in all 19 runs (reference, edge_predict, 17 judge runs). The module also equals an independent implementation of the inventory rule on 3,000 synthetic tie-heavy inputs, including last-group merges.
cites: inventory train.sas printed_hosmer_lemeshow.csv row (DF = NGroups - 2); RULEBOOK §2 numeric missing row ('polars null (never NaN)'); RULEBOOK §2 UNKNOWN rule; scratch sc-review-B/hl_ctable.py, hl_edge.py
fix: Return None (not NaN) for the p-value when DF < 1, and add TODO(port): 'SAS output for LACKFIT with fewer than 3 groups unverified'.

finding: roc_association and association_table (:643) divide by C + D for Gamma, so they raise ZeroDivisionError when every pair is tied. With one class empty, p = 0 raises and n1 or n0 = 0 breaks the DeLong variance. With n1 = 1 or n0 = 1, np.var(ddof=1) is NaN, so StdErr and CI are NaN, not missing. The inventory says both classes are present on every receivable input, but the helpers themselves state no precondition.
cites: inventory metrics_calculation.sas gini row ('both classes present in every receivable input'); RULEBOOK §2 numeric missing row (never NaN); RULEBOOK §2 UNKNOWN rule
fix: Return None for undefined statistics, or raise a clear error, with a TODO(port) on SAS's behaviour.

finding: The D-format helpers choose the magnitude branch BEFORE rounding and do not handle width overflow. sas_d12_3(9999.9999996) gives '10000.000000', though the rule says |x| >= 1e4 prints 0 decimals. sas_d12_3(99.99999951) gives '100.000000'. sas_d8(123456789.0) gives '123456789' (9 chars in D8.). The TODO at :272 says |x| < 1e-5 was 'never observed', but it is reachable: Percent Tied falls below 1e-5 % with 68 or fewer tied pairs out of 686,727,936, and 0 ties prints '0' (unverified). All 2,406 SAS D12.3 cells and all 240 PVALUE6.4 cells in reference + runs reproduce.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 helper verification (A31: D12.3 magnitudes never observed get explicit cases); inventory train.sas printed_association.csv row (D12.3 rule); scratch sc-review-B/formats.py
fix: Pick the branch from the value rounded at the branch's decimals. Fall back to E-notation when the text exceeds w. Extend the TODO(port) at :272 to say Percent Tied reaches |x| < 1e-5 when ties <= 68.

cites: RULEBOOK §2 helper verification (A31: 'the D12.3 magnitudes never observed (100 <= |x| < 1e4, |x| < 1e-5)' get explicit cases)
fix: Report it as OPEN/TODO outside the PASS count. Or add an ODA experiment, as the inventory printed_association.csv row asks ('verify with an ODA experiment in the Step 2 sas_compat pilot').

finding: The comparisons are not self-referential: judge_file calls the judge's compare.compare_file(name, ref, cand, 'port') against judge/reference with the real tolerances. But port tolerance is the wrong bar when the input is SAS's OWN pd (check_reference_pd_tables :447, hl_and_assoc :423, check_roc :456). The inventory rows claim BYTE-IDENTICAL output there, yet port mode allows HL Totals/Observed ±2, D8 cells 2 display units + 0.1 %, and Score chi-squares 2 du + 1e-3 relative (±14.5 at step 1). A grouping off-by-2 or a 1-unit formatting slip would still pass. I re-ran these exactly: HL is byte-identical in 19/19 runs, ROC in 51/51 files, and stepwise chi-squares agree with my independent numpy to 1.3e-12 relative. So nothing is hidden today, but the script cannot prove it.
cites: inventory train.sas printed_hl_partition.csv row ('the rule writes judge/reference/printed_hl_partition.csv BYTE-IDENTICALLY'), printed_roc_train.csv row ('BYTE-IDENTICAL to the reference'); judge/compare.py:114-127,250-279 (port tolerances)
fix: For SAS-pd inputs, compare text exactly (compare_file(..., 'strict') or ==). Keep port mode only for the converged-fit candidates.

finding: Every procedure check uses one input, judge/reference (plus edge a/b/c for ROC). The 17 SAS runs in judge/runs (5 feature mutations, slentry=0.10, slstay=0.10, a split-drift run) are never used, and they are exactly where B-01 (ctable grid: 44 vs 46 rows) and B-02 (D8 E-notation: 5 cells) show up. cites: RULEBOOK §2 helper verification (A31: 'Helper branches that no judged input reaches get explicit cases in the Step 2 sas_compat review'); judge/runs/*/ (SAS 9.4 outputs)
fix: Loop the stepwise/HL/ctable/ROC/D8 checks over every judge/runs dir with model_features_train.csv, using that run's slentry/slstay. Add synthetic unit cases for the listed branches (see scratch sc-review-B/edge_fit.py, hl_edge.py).
